card.band: 4 h. A frontier agent can implement known methods and ensemble them, which beats the baseline. The hidden family gap limits the mean. A weaker model stops at the baseline.
card.cheat: Memorising dataset identity from features: the hidden families are disjoint and their features are not shipped.
card.grading: AUROC and FPR95 on hidden near-OOD and far-OOD dataset families that are not given to the agent. The score is normalised between the shipped MSP baseline and our reference.
card.reference: The best of the repo's published post-hoc methods (such as ViM, KNN, ensemble variants), re-run on the same cached features. The scores are measured. Data licences must be checked per dataset, and none is verified yet.
card.task: /app ships a scoped OpenOOD v1.5 evaluation code with small, pre-trained CPU-sized classifiers and cached features for a few in-distribution sets. The agent designs and tunes an OOD scoring method (combining logit, feature and density signals) with a dev split. Interface: a Python scoring function over features.
card.title: Post-hoc OOD detector design on small CPU-trained classifiers with a dataset-family split

history: The reference is the best of the repo's own published post-hoc methods (ViM, KNN, ensemble), which already sit in openood/postprocessors at v1.5. A frontier agent can copy and blend them and reach the reference quickly, so the task is too easy. The grading surface is also small (few hidden families)
source_notes: MIT licence fits shipping. Likely GPU-heavy for CIFAR/ImageNet-scale training, so CPU fit is doubtful and needs a small-model scoped variant. Benchmark datasets are not bundled in the repo, so data licences must be checked separately. Not on the already_known list.

v1.kill_reason: The reference is the best of the repo's own published post-hoc methods (ViM, KNN, ensemble), which already sit in openood/postprocessors at v1.5. A frontier agent can copy and blend them and reach the reference quickly, so the task is too easy. The grading surface is also small (few hidden families), and the reference is readable upstream, so sealing is weak.

Band.why: Upstream code already gives the reference; a frontier agent reaches it fast, so the scope is too easy

Build.why: Estimated about 3 days for licence checks, feature caching and the hidden-family harness

Fit.why: Fits CPU if the scope is only the scoring stage on cached features

Hor.why: Scoring-function design over cached features is a few hours of work, not long-horizon

Lic.why: Repo is MIT; per-dataset licences are unverified

Multi.why: Essentially one lever (choice and blend of scores); little independent partial credit

Nov.why: Max neighbour cosine 0.167 (S-rs-017), above the 0.15 threshold; not a crowded task but close to a neighbour

Real.why: Well-known OpenOOD repo at v1.5 with a peer-reviewed benchmark paper

Ref.why: Reference is measured, but it is the best of existing upstream methods rather than a complete new implementation

Seal.why: The reference methods are public upstream code in the shipped repo, so the reference is readable

Surf.why: Few hidden dataset families give tens of cases, not thousands or an unlimited generator

spike_plan.kill_if: Upstream ViM/KNN/ensemble matches the best achievable score on dev within about 0.01 AUROC, or any candidate OOD dataset is not licence-clear for shipping. Either way kill as K8 (too easy) or K6.
spike_plan.pass_if: The best upstream method is clearly beaten (by at least 0.02 AUROC) on held-out families by a new combination that is not in upstream, AND the hidden-family gap is measurable.
steps: Clone OpenOOD v1.5 into a throwaway container with network; confirm the commit and the postprocessors directory.
Run the upstream ViM, KNN and ensemble postprocessors on the cached CIFAR-10 features with a small CPU classifier; check that they run and are deterministic over repeated runs.
Using a stand-in set of far-OOD features (e.g. public SVHN/Textures, only if licence allows), compute AUROC and FPR95 for MSP, ViM, KNN and their ensemble.
Compare the best upstream combination with a simple learned blend on a dev split to see whether there is headroom above the reference.
Check per-dataset licences for the candidate OOD sets before any further work.

v1.summary: The OpenOOD v1.5 repo (MIT) and its post-hoc methods (ViM, KNN, ensemble) are confirmed as public upstream code, so the reference is directly available and a frontier agent can reach it without novel work. The task is killed as K8 (too easy), with a weak seal and a small hidden-family grading surface as secondary concerns.
